## Introduction

The Green Transit Alliance (GTA) awards those public transit agencies that performs well in reducing carbon emissions. Here the objective is to compare the emissions produced by public transit agencies with the emission that would have been generated from private vehicles if made the same routes across the United States. 

The analysis used data from the U.S. Energy Information Administrative (EIA) and the National Transit Database (NTD) to estimate the transit emissions. The study reveals that the relationship between fuel type and emissions is not always predictable. 

## Data Acquisition

### State Electricity Profiles

```{r}
#| label: eia-sep-download
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)
library(fs)
library(gt)

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
  
    state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
    
    dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
    file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
    
    fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
    
    if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
        BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
        RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
          req_url_path("electricity", 
                       "state", 
                       state_formatted) |>
          req_headers(
            `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>   
          req_retry(
                max_tries = 4, 
          ) |>
          req_perform(file_name)
    
        resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
    }
    
    TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
        html_element("table") |> 
        html_table() |>
        mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
    
    if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
        TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
    }
    
    CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |> 
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
        pull(Rank)
    
    RATE <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        as.numeric()
    
    GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
               primary_source        = PRIMARY,
               electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
               # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
               generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
               state                 = state, 
               abbreviation          = abbr
    )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()
```
The electricity data generated from the U.S. Energy Information administration (EIA) State Electricity Profiles includes four main variables: CO2 emissions per MWh, the state's primary energy source, net electricity generation in MWh, and the average retail electricity price. The price was converted from cents per kWh to dollars per MWh to make the units easier to comprehend. 

The analysis assumes the state's overall energy emissions rate rather than a separate rate for each agency to provide a consistent estimate using state-level data. The data set covers all 50 states, excluding Washington, D.C. 

### NTD Energy Usage

```{r}
#| label: ntd-energy-download
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()
```

```{r}
#| label: ntd-service-download
load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```
The transit energy data from the National Transit Database (NTD) reports the consumption of energy by public transportation agencies, including  diesel, gasoline, natural gas, and electricity for 2025. Each row represents one agency and one mode, for example NYC Transit's buses. The Bio-diesel description column was dropped from the calculation because it describes what type of bio-diesel was used rather than the amount. Fuel is measured in gallons, electricity in kWh, and hydrogen in kg. 

The 2025 NTD service data set was provides the information about passenger trips (UTP) and passenger miles traveled. The UTP counts each passenger boarding. A transfer to another vehicle counts as two trips. 

These combined data sets help to compare the energy consumption against the amount of transportation services provided.


## Data Cleaning and Preparation

### Recoding Transit Modes

```{r}
#| label: recode-mode
# Translate NTD two-letter mode codes into readable names.
# Defined once as a function so both NTD tables are recoded identically.
recode_mode <- function(x) {
  recode_values(x,
    "AR" ~ "Alaska Railroad",
    "CB" ~ "Commuter Bus",
    "CC" ~ "Cable Car",
    "CR" ~ "Commuter Rail",
    "DR" ~ "Demand Response",
    "FB" ~ "Ferryboat",
    "HR" ~ "Heavy Rail",
    "IP" ~ "Inclined Plane",
    "LR" ~ "Light Rail",
    "MB" ~ "Bus",
    "MG" ~ "Monorail / Automated Guideway",
    "RB" ~ "Bus Rapid Transit",
    "SR" ~ "Streetcar Rail",
    "TB" ~ "Trolleybus",
    "TR" ~ "Aerial Tramway",
    "VP" ~ "Vanpool",
    "YR" ~ "Hybrid Rail",
    default = "Unknown"
  )
}

NTD_SERVICE <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(mode = recode_mode(mode))
```


```{r}
#| label: recode-mode-energy
NTD_ENERGY <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(Mode = recode_mode(Mode))
```

The NTD data set uses two-letter mode codes such as, MB represent Bus, and HR represent Heavy Rail which were converted into readable name using the [NTD ridership data page](https://catalog-beta.data.gov/dataset/complete-monthly-ridership-with-adjustments-and-estimates). 

The same recoding function was applied to both the service and energy datasets to ensure transit mode names match and keeps the name consistent. All codes were successfully matched, with no “Unknown” values because mode is part of the key used to join the tables.

#### National Average Emissions

##### The Calculation

```{r}
#| label: us-avg-co2
# Weight each state's emissions rate by how much electricity it generates
us_avg_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  summarize(avg = weighted.mean(CO2_MWh, w = generation_MWh)) |>
  pull(avg)

# Unweighted average, for comparison
us_simple_avg_co2 <- mean(EIA_SEP_REPORT$CO2_MWh)
```

The average CO₂ emissions rate from US electricity generation, weighted by how much electricity each state produces, was `r scales::comma(us_avg_co2, accuracy = 1)` pounds of CO₂ per MWh. This means that the average emissions rate reflects the electricity generated across the country rather than treating every state equally. Compared with the cleanest and dirtiest states in the dataset, this national average provides a useful benchmark for understanding differences in electricity-related emissions.

#### Texas vs. New York

```{r}
#| label: tx-vs-ny
tx_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "TX") |> pull(CO2_MWh)
ny_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "NY") |> pull(CO2_MWh)

# How many times more CO2 Texas emits per MWh than New York
tx_ny_ratio <- tx_co2 / ny_co2
```

Texas produces `r round(tx_ny_ratio, 1)` times as much CO₂ per MWh of electricity as New York. This means New York's electricity generation is substantially cleaner than Texas's.

## Data Analysis
## Calculating Emissions
### Preparing Service Data

```{r}
#| label: service-agg
# Collapse service to one row per agency + mode
# (combining directly operated and purchased transportation)
SERVICE_AGG <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, AGENCY, city, state, uza_name, mode) |>
  summarize(
    total_upt      = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_miles    = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    miles_reported = any(!is.na(sum_passenger_miles)),
    any_flagged    = any(flagged_likely_inaccurate),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### Combining the Data

```{r}
#| label: combine-data
# Energy: match the service table's ID format ("00001") and column names
ENERGY_CLEAN <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(NTD_ID = sprintf("%05d", as.integer(`NTD ID`))) |>
  select(-`NTD ID`, -`Agency Name`, -`Bio-Diesel Description`) |>
  rename(mode = Mode)

# EIA: keep only what the emissions calculation needs
EIA_CO2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  select(abbreviation, CO2_MWh)

# One row per agency + mode with service, fuel use, and grid emissions
EMISSIONS_BASE <- SERVICE_AGG |>
  inner_join(ENERGY_CLEAN,
             join_by(NTD_ID, mode),
             relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  inner_join(EIA_CO2,
             join_by(state == abbreviation),
             relationship = "many-to-one")
```

### Emissions per Agency and Mode

```{r}
#| label: compute-emissions
# Pounds of CO2 per unit of fuel (EIA, plus documented assumptions)
LBS_CO2 <- c(
  diesel    = 22.45,  # per gallon, distillate fuel oil
  gasoline  = 18.73,  # per gallon, finished motor gasoline
  kerosene  = 21.78,  # per gallon
  lpg       = 12.68,  # per gallon, propane
  bunker    = 24.78,  # per gallon, residual fuel oil
  biodiesel = 22.45,  # per gallon, assumed equal to diesel (conservative)
  ethanol   = 3.13,   # per gallon, assumed E85 (15% gasoline share)
  cng       = 15.31,  # per gasoline gallon equivalent
  lng       = 9.89,   # per gallon
  hydrogen  = 0       # per kg, no tailpipe CO2
)

EMISSIONS <- EMISSIONS_BASE |>
  mutate(
    # Direct (tailpipe) emissions from combustion fuels
    co2_fuel_lbs =
      `Gallons of Diesel Fuel`             * LBS_CO2["diesel"] +
      `Gallons of Gasoline`                * LBS_CO2["gasoline"] +
      `Gallons of Kerosene`                * LBS_CO2["kerosene"] +
      `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas` * LBS_CO2["lpg"] +
      `Gallons of Bunker Fuel`             * LBS_CO2["bunker"] +
      `Gallons of Bio-Diesel`              * LBS_CO2["biodiesel"] +
      `Gallons of Ethanol`                 * LBS_CO2["ethanol"] +
      `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`  * LBS_CO2["cng"] +
      `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`       * LBS_CO2["lng"] +
      `Kilograms of Hydrogen`              * LBS_CO2["hydrogen"],
    # Upstream emissions from electricity (kWh -> MWh x state rate)
    co2_elec_lbs =
      (`Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery` +
       `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`) / 1000 * CO2_MWh,
    total_co2_lbs  = co2_fuel_lbs + co2_elec_lbs,
    total_co2_tons = total_co2_lbs / 2000
  )
```

### Emissions per Rider

```{r}
#| label: agency-emissions
# Combine modes into one row per agency, then normalize by usage.
# Exclude NTD-flagged records and agencies with unreported miles,
# since either would distort per-trip or per-mile figures.
AGENCY_EMISSIONS <- EMISSIONS |>
  filter(!any_flagged) |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, AGENCY, city, state) |>
  summarize(
    total_co2_lbs   = sum(total_co2_lbs),
    co2_elec_lbs    = sum(co2_elec_lbs),
    total_upt       = sum(total_upt),
    total_miles     = sum(total_miles),
    miles_complete  = all(miles_reported),
    n_modes         = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(miles_complete, total_upt > 0, total_miles > 0) |>
  mutate(
    agency_short = str_remove(AGENCY, ".*dba:\\s*"),
    co2_per_upt  = total_co2_lbs / total_upt,
    co2_per_mile = total_co2_lbs / total_miles
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: agency-size
# Exclude very small agencies, then assign award size categories
AGENCY_EMISSIONS <- AGENCY_EMISSIONS |>
  filter(total_upt >= 100000) |>
  mutate(
    size = case_when(
      total_upt <  1e6 ~ "Small",
      total_upt < 1e7  ~ "Medium",
      TRUE             ~ "Large"
    ),
    size = factor(size, levels = c("Small", "Medium", "Large"))
  )
```

## Award Winners

### Greenest Agency

```{r}
#| label: award-greenest
# Lowest CO2 per passenger mile in each size category,
# compared with the median agency of the same size
GREENEST <- AGENCY_EMISSIONS |>
  group_by(size) |>
  mutate(median_per_mile = median(co2_per_mile)) |>
  slice_min(co2_per_mile, n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(times_cleaner = median_per_mile / co2_per_mile)

GREENEST |>
  select(size, agency_short, city, state,
         co2_per_mile, median_per_mile, times_cleaner) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    size            = "Category",
    agency_short    = "Agency",
    city            = "City",
    state           = "State",
    co2_per_mile    = "Winner (lbs CO\u2082 / passenger mile)",
    median_per_mile = "Median Agency",
    times_cleaner   = "Times Cleaner"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(co2_per_mile, median_per_mile), decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_number(columns = times_cleaner, decimals = 1, pattern = "{x}\u00d7") |>
  tab_header(title = "Greenest Transit Agencies of 2025") |>
  tab_source_note(
    "Sources: National Transit Database (2025); US Energy Information Administration"
  )
```

### Most Emissions Avoided

```{r}
#| label: award-avoided
# Fuel economy of the counterfactual car (NHTSA CAFE target, MY2026).
# Generous to cars: real-world mpg is lower, so savings are conservative.
CAFE_MPG <- 49

AGENCY_EMISSIONS <- AGENCY_EMISSIONS |>
  mutate(
    # CO2 if every passenger mile had been driven alone in a car
    driving_co2_lbs = total_miles / CAFE_MPG * LBS_CO2["gasoline"],
    avoided_co2_lbs = driving_co2_lbs - total_co2_lbs,
    avoided_tons    = avoided_co2_lbs / 2000
  )

MOST_AVOIDED <- AGENCY_EMISSIONS |>
  group_by(size) |>
  mutate(median_avoided = median(avoided_tons)) |>
  slice_max(avoided_tons, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()

MOST_AVOIDED |>
  select(size, agency_short, city, state, avoided_tons, median_avoided) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    size           = "Category",
    agency_short   = "Agency",
    city           = "City",
    state          = "State",
    avoided_tons   = "CO\u2082 Avoided (tons)",
    median_avoided = "Median Agency (tons)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(avoided_tons, median_avoided), decimals = 0) |>
  tab_header(title = "Most Emissions Avoided in 2025") |>
  tab_source_note(
    "Assumes each passenger mile replaces a solo car trip at 49 mpg (NHTSA CAFE, MY2026). Sources: NTD (2025); EIA; NHTSA"
  )
```

### Worst Offender

```{r}
#| label: award-worst
# Pounds of CO2 per mile for a solo car at the CAFE target
CAR_LBS_PER_MILE <- LBS_CO2["gasoline"] / CAFE_MPG

# Highest CO2 per passenger mile among Medium and Large agencies
WORST <- AGENCY_EMISSIONS |>
  filter(size %in% c("Medium", "Large")) |>
  group_by(size) |>
  mutate(median_per_mile = median(co2_per_mile)) |>
  slice_max(co2_per_mile, n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(times_car = co2_per_mile / CAR_LBS_PER_MILE)

WORST |>
  select(size, agency_short, city, state,
         co2_per_mile, median_per_mile, times_car) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    size            = "Category",
    agency_short    = "Agency",
    city            = "City",
    state           = "State",
    co2_per_mile    = "lbs CO\u2082 / passenger mile",
    median_per_mile = "Median Agency",
    times_car       = "vs. Driving Alone"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(co2_per_mile, median_per_mile), decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_number(columns = times_car, decimals = 1, pattern = "{x}\u00d7") |>
  tab_header(title = "Worst Offenders of 2025") |>
  tab_source_note(
    "Driving benchmark: solo car at 49 mpg (NHTSA CAFE, MY2026). Sources: NTD (2025); EIA; NHTSA"
  )
```

## Press Release Graphics

```{r}
#| label: fig-greenest-worst
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
library(ggrepel)

# Mark which agencies won Greenest or Worst Offender
highlight <- bind_rows(
  GREENEST |> mutate(award = "Greenest"),
  WORST    |> mutate(award = "Worst Offender")
) |>
  select(NTD_ID, award)

plot_data <- AGENCY_EMISSIONS |>
  left_join(highlight, join_by(NTD_ID)) |>
  mutate(award = replace_na(award, "Other agencies"))

others  <- plot_data |> filter(award == "Other agencies")
winners <- plot_data |> filter(award != "Other agencies")

set.seed(9750)  # keeps the dot scatter identical on every render

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = co2_per_mile, y = size)) +
  # All other agencies as faint grey dots
  geom_jitter(data = others, height = 0.2, width = 0,
              colour = "grey70", alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  # Car benchmark line
  geom_vline(xintercept = unname(CAR_LBS_PER_MILE),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = unname(CAR_LBS_PER_MILE), y = 3.45,
           label = "Driving alone (49 mpg car)",
           hjust = -0.05, size = 4, colour = "grey30") +
  # Award winners, highlighted and labelled
  geom_point(data = winners, aes(colour = award), size = 4) +
  geom_label_repel(data = winners,
                   aes(label = agency_short, colour = award),
                   size = 3.5, show.legend = FALSE,
                   min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.6) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.01)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Greenest"       = "#1b7837",
                                 "Worst Offender" = "#b2182b")) +
  labs(
    title    = "The Greenest and Dirtiest Transit Agencies of 2025",
        subtitle = "CO2 per passenger mile for every agency; dots left of the dashed line beat driving alone",
    x        = "lbs CO2 per passenger mile (log scale)",
    y        = NULL,
    colour   = NULL,
    caption  = "Sources: National Transit Database (2025); US EIA; NHTSA CAFE standards"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "top",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
